# sigma_member (Resource)

A Sigma member (user). Destroying this resource deactivates the user (Sigma retains audit history); it is not a hard delete.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# member_type is the account type's canonical license name. Use the value Sigma
# stores (e.g. "build", "view", "admin") — note Sigma normalizes some UI labels
# (the "Creator" account type is stored as "build"), so passing "creator" here
# causes an "inconsistent result after apply" error. Use "build".
resource "sigma_member" "alice" {
  email       = "alice@example.com"
  first_name  = "Alice"
  last_name   = "Anderson"
  member_type = "build"
  user_kind   = "internal"
}

# Destroying this resource deactivates Alice (Sigma retains audit history);
# it is not a hard delete.

# Silent provisioning: skip the invitation email at create time, e.g. when an
# external IdP (Okta/Azure AD) handles user onboarding.
resource "sigma_member" "bot" {
  email       = "svc-bot@example.com"
  first_name  = "Service"
  last_name   = "Bot"
  member_type = "build"
  send_invite = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) Member's email address. Must be unique within the org.
- `first_name` (String) First name.
- `last_name` (String) Last name.

### Optional

- `format_region` (String) Region whose number, date and currency conventions apply, e.g. `US`, `GB`, `JP` (Beta).
- `language` (String) Preferred display language, e.g. `EN`, `DE_DE`, `JA_JA` (Beta). See the Sigma API reference for the full list.
- `member_type` (String) Account type's canonical license name as Sigma stores it (e.g. 'admin', 'build', 'view', or a custom account type name). Note: Sigma normalizes some UI labels — the "Creator" account type is stored as 'build' — so passing the UI label (e.g. 'creator') causes an "inconsistent result after apply" error. Use the stored value. If omitted, Sigma applies the organization's Invitation default account type (Admin > Account types); the assigned value is then read back into state.
- `send_invite` (Boolean) Whether Sigma should email an invitation to the new member. Defaults to `true` (Sigma's API default). Set to `false` for silent provisioning (e.g. when an external IdP handles user onboarding). **Only applied at create time** — changes to this attribute on an existing member are ignored. To suppress the diff after flipping it post-creation, use `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [send_invite] }`.
- `user_kind` (String) One of `internal`, `guest`, `embed`. Defaults to `internal` server-side.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) RFC3339 timestamp of member creation.
- `created_by` (String) Identifier of the member who created this member.
- `home_folder_id` (String) UUID of the user's My Documents folder.
- `id` (String) Sigma member identifier (`memberId`). Opaque string; not necessarily a UUID.
- `organization_id` (String) Sigma organization UUID this member belongs to.
- `profile_img_url` (String) URL of the user's profile image, or empty.
- `updated_at` (String) RFC3339 timestamp of last update.
- `updated_by` (String) Identifier of the member who last updated this member.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sigma_member.example '<member_id>'
```
